docs.title: Celebi
docs.text:
Time-Travel Harness for LLM API Streams

Celebi is a man-in-the-middle proxy that sits between your coding agent and LLM providers. It captures every request/response pair in a graph database, forming a timeline of conversations that you can visualize, search, and replay.

Named after the time-traveling Pokemon — because debugging LLMs should feel like time travel.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Go to GitHub Releases to download the latest installer.

Platform File Guide macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) celebi-*-macos.dmg Install Guide Linux (Debian / Ubuntu) celebi_*_amd64.deb Install Guide Windows (x64) celebi-*-windows-setup.exe Install Guide

docs.title: What does Celebi do?
docs.text:
• Captures every API call between your agent and the LLM
  • Stores conversations as a directed graph (prompt → response nodes)
  • Visualizes the full conversation flow in a card-based graph view
  • Replays any prompt to compare outputs
  • Searches across all stored conversations by content
  • Tracks token usage per request for cost analysis

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Technology Purpose Desktop GUI PySide6 (Qt6) Setup wizard, graph visualization, search, analytics Proxy Server FastAPI + Uvicorn Intercepts and forwards LLM API requests LLM Gateway LiteLLM Unified interface to multiple LLM providers Graph Database Kuzu Stores conversation timeline as a directed graph HTTP Client httpx Async streaming proxy between Celebi and LLM

docs.title: Graph Schema
docs.text:
State (node)
├── id: UUID
├── step_type: "prompt" | "response"
└── payload: JSON string

Edges
├── TRANSITIONED_TO: prompt -> response (linear flow)
└── BRANCHED_TO: parent_prompt -> new_prompt (replay/branch)

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Agent sends request → Celebi interceptor captures the full request body
  2. Prompt stored → Creates a State node with step_type="prompt"
  3. Request forwarded → Proxied to LiteLLM, then to the LLM provider
  4. Response captured → Streaming response is assembled and stored
  5. Response stored → Creates a State node with step_type="response"
  6. Edge created → TRANSITIONED_TO edge connects prompt to response
  7. Response returned → Agent receives the response as if Celebi wasn't there

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or higher
  • uv package manager
  • Git

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Fork and clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/celebi-harness.git
cd celebi-harness

# Install dependencies
uv sync

# Run linting
uv run ruff check celebi/

# Run the GUI
python -m celebi

docs.title: 1. Create a Branch
docs.text: git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name

docs.title: 2. Make Changes
docs.text:
• Follow the Coding Standards
  • Write tests for new functionality
  • Update documentation if needed

docs.title: 3. Test Your Changes
docs.text:
# Linting
uv run ruff check celebi/
uv run ruff format --check celebi/

# Auto-fix
uv run ruff check --fix celebi/
uv run ruff format celebi/

docs.title: 4. Commit and Push
docs.text:
git add .
git commit -m "feat: add new feature"
git push origin feature/your-feature-name

docs.title: Python Style
docs.text:
• Formatter/Linter: Ruff
  • Line Length: 100 characters
  • Quotes: Double quotes
  • Import Sorting: Ruff isort

docs.title: 1. Launch Celebi
docs.text: After installing, open Celebi from your application launcher or terminal.

docs.title: 2. Setup Wizard
docs.text: The first time you launch Celebi, you'll see the setup wizard.

docs.title: Page 1 — Select Project
docs.text:
• Project Name: A name for this project (e.g., "my-app")
  • Project Folder: Browse to your project directory
  • Agent: Select your coding agent (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, or Kiro)

docs.title: Page 2 — Provider Credentials
docs.text:
• Provider: Select your LLM provider (Gemini, OpenAI, or Anthropic)
  • API Key: Enter your API key
  • Click Fetch Models to load available models
  • Select a model from the dropdown

docs.title: 3. Start the Proxy
docs.text:
Click Start on the dashboard. Celebi will:

  1. Start a LiteLLM gateway on port 4000
  2. Start the FastAPI proxy on port 8000
  3. Generate the agent config file in your project folder

docs.title: 4. Use Your Agent
docs.text: Open your coding agent in the project folder as usual. All LLM requests will be transparently captured by Celebi.

docs.title: 5. Inspect Conversations
docs.text:
Use the Celebi dashboard to:

  • Graph: View the conversation flow as a node graph
  • Search: Find specific prompts or responses
  • Analytics: Track token usage and costs

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
# Check the proxy is running
curl http://localhost:8000/
# Expected: {"message":"Hello Traveller"}

# Check the graph
curl http://localhost:8000/graph
# Expected: {"nodes":0,"edges":0,"data":[]}

docs.title: Supported Agents
docs.text: Celebi generates agent-specific configuration files so your coding agent routes through the proxy automatically.

docs.title: Supported Agents
docs.text: Agent Config File Description OpenCode opencode.json AI-native coding agent Claude Code .claude/settings.json Anthropic's CLI coding agent Codex .codex/config.json OpenAI's Codex CLI Kiro .kiro/config.json AWS's AI IDE

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: When you select an agent during setup, Celebi writes a configuration file to your project folder that redirects the agent's LLM requests through the Celebi proxy.

docs.title: OpenCode
docs.text:
Celebi writes an opencode.json in your project root:

{
  "provider": {
    "celebi": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Celebi Proxy",
      "options": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:8000" },
      "models": { "your-model": { "name": "your-model (via Celebi)" } }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
Celebi writes .claude/settings.json:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:8000/v1",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "your-model"
  }
}

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
Celebi writes .codex/config.json:

{
  "model": "your-model",
  "api_base": "http://localhost:8000/v1"
}

docs.title: Kiro
docs.text:
Celebi writes .kiro/config.json:

{
  "provider": {
    "endpoint": "http://localhost:8000",
    "model": "your-model"
  }
}

docs.title: Adding a New Agent
docs.text:
To add support for a new agent:

  1. Add a writer function in celebi/agents.py
  2. Register it in the AGENTS dictionary
  3. The setup wizard will automatically pick it up

docs.title: Install Celebi
docs.text: Choose your platform below to install Celebi.

docs.title: All Platforms
docs.text: Platform Format Guide macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) .dmg disk image macOS Install Guide Linux (Debian / Ubuntu) .deb package Linux Install Guide Windows (x64) .exe installer Windows Install Guide

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Go to GitHub Releases to download the latest installer for your platform.

Platform File macOS celebi-*-macos.dmg Linux celebi_*_amd64.deb Windows celebi-*-windows-setup.exe

Each release includes SHA256 checksums (.sha256 files) for verification.

docs.title: Verifying Downloads
docs.text:
# Linux / macOS
sha256sum -c celebi-<version>-<platform>.sha256

# Windows (PowerShell)
Get-FileHash celebi-*-windows-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256

docs.title: Download
docs.text: Download the latest .deb package from GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Install with dpkg
docs.text:
sudo dpkg -i celebi_0.1.0_amd64.deb
sudo apt-get install -f  # fix any missing dependencies

docs.title: Install with apt (from local file)
docs.text: sudo apt install ./celebi_0.1.0_amd64.deb

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
# From terminal
celebi

# Or find it in your application launcher

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Verify the proxy starts
curl http://localhost:8000/
# Expected: {"message":"Hello Traveller"}

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The .deb package requires these system libraries (usually pre-installed):

  • libegl1 — EGL rendering
  • libgl1 — OpenGL
  • libxkbcommon0 — keyboard handling
  • libdbus-1-3 — D-Bus IPC

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
sudo dpkg -r celebi

Optionally remove the config directory:

rm -rf ~/.celebi

docs.title: Download
docs.text: Download the latest .dmg installer from GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Open the downloaded .dmg file
  2. Drag Celebi into the Applications folder
  3. Eject the disk image

docs.title: First Launch
docs.text:
On first launch, macOS may show a security warning because the app is not notarized. To allow it:

  1. Click OK on the warning dialog
  2. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security
  3. Scroll down and click Open Anyway next to the Celebi warning
  4. Click Open in the confirmation dialog

Alternatively, you can bypass Gatekeeper from the terminal:

xattr -cr /Applications/Celebi.app

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Launch from terminal
/Applications/Celebi.app/Contents/MacOS/celebi

# Or verify the proxy starts
curl http://localhost:8000/
# Expected: {"message":"Hello Traveller"}

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
1. Drag Celebi from Applications to Trash
  2. Optionally remove the config directory: 
    rm -rf ~/.celebi

docs.title: Download
docs.text: Download the latest celebi-*-windows-setup.exe from GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Run the downloaded .exe installer
  2. Click Next on the welcome screen
  3. Accept the license agreement
  4. Choose the install location (default: C:\Program Files\Celebi)
  5. Click Install
  6. Click Finish to launch Celebi

docs.title: First Launch
docs.text:
Windows Defender SmartScreen may show a warning because the app is not code-signed. To allow it:

  1. Click More info on the SmartScreen dialog
  2. Click Run anyway

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Verify the proxy starts
Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/
# Expected: {"message":"Hello Traveller"}

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Apps → Installed apps
  2. Find Celebi and click Uninstall
  3. Follow the uninstaller prompts

Or use the uninstaller shortcut in Start Menu → Celebi → Uninstall.

Optionally remove the config directory:

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force ~\.celebi
